newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close up on active secondaries.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close up on active secondaries.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed higher in moderate trade on Thursday on the back of active buying of medium- and small-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.74 points, or 0.69 percent, to close at 546.46 points. Gainers led losers by 62 to 34, with 50 counters unchanged.

Brokers said trade in the second session was more active due to fresh buying of certain counters although sentiment remain volatile as many operators were cautious about the implications of the new minimum reserve ratios set for banks.
"More positive news on selected counters and a little support from regional markets had stimulated fresh buying," one local broker said.
On Wednesday, the central bank announced that the minimum reserve requirement ratio of banks will be raised to five percent from three percent effective April 16, 1997.

Tyre maker Gajah Tunggal and tyre-cord producer Andayani Megah of the Gajah Tunggal group, were actively traded on what brokers said was speculation of upcoming rights issues. Gajah Tunggal topped the active list, rising 100 rupiah to 1,100 on 9.5 million shares while Andayani Megah rose 100 rupiah to 1,150.
Shipping firm Berlian Laju Tanker rose 200 rupiah to 2,600 on a volume of 4.9 million shares. Brokers said the rise was due to market talk of a possible link-up with a foreign firm.
Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma and its distribution firm Enseval were also actively traded on what brokers said were good earnings prospects coupled with low prevailing prices.
Kalbe Farma rose 375 rupiah, or 8.33 percent, to 4,875 rupiah on a volume of 1.1 million shares. Enseval rose 125 rupiah, or 11.11 percent, to 1,250 on a turnover of 1.8 million shares.
Bank Mashill Utama was also actively traded, up 250 rupiah to 2,350 rupiah on a volume of 2.6 million shares on market talk of a possible merger with another listed bank.
